mechanism: Heisenberg conjugation of a beam-splitter generator by a full (pi) beam splitter; exact passive-unitary identity, layout-preserving

rule.name: diagonal_hop_by_full_bs_conjugation_via_common_neighbor
rule.idea: Hop between two qumodes that are not grid-coupled (e.g. the diagonal pairs (0,3) and (1,2) on a 2x2 qumode grid) is synthesized without any SWAP by conjugating a full (pi) beam splitter on a common coupled neighbor m. Let G_{xy}(q) = e^{iq} a_x^+ a_y + h.c., BS_{xy}(t,q) = exp(-i t/2 G_{xy}(q)), and W = BS_{j,m}(-pi, 0) = exp(+i pi/2 (a_j^+ a_m + h.c.)). The Heisenberg map for theta=-pi/2 gives W^+ a_m W = i a_j and W^+ a_j W = i a_m, while W leaves a_l untouched. Hence W^+ G_{m,l}(q) W = G_{j,l}(q - pi/2), so W^+ BS_{m,l}(t, p + pi/2) W = BS_{j,l}(t, p) exactly, on the full three-mode Fock space, for every t and p and regardless of photon number. The gate sequence in time order is BS_{j,m}(-pi,0), BS_{m,l}(t, p+pi/2), BS_{j,m}(+pi,0): 3 two-mode gates, 0 one-mode gates, 0 SWAPs, replacing the router's layout-permuting SWAP insertion for non-adjacent hops. The outer BS_{j,m}(+-pi,0) gates are exact inverses of (or equal to) native full hops already adjacent in the circuit, enabling a later BS inverse-pair cancellation.

reason: rule never chosen/applied on any benchmark
